source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: Theorem2.13 adaptive weighted-potential extension, Eq.(4.4), Theorem4.14 and separate minimum/infimum repair.

blindSetup.variables: Every free variable in a row and its expanded hypotheses is universally quantified, with fixed parameters held equal across a run. Units 2 and 3 (when E occurs) use an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its normed additive commutative group. V is an OnlineGradientDescent.Domain on E, x_init∈E (the Lean parameter x₁, which is the time-0 output), ℓ:ℕ→E→extended reals, p a SupportPolicy, α,D real, t,T natural, u∈E. Write x∈V for membership in V.carrier. Unlisted feasibility, convexity, or sign premises are not implicit. Numbering is zero-based.
blindSetup.run: At time 0, H₀=(x_init), S₀=0. At time t, state A_t=(H_t,S_t), H_t has t+1 entries, x_t=H_t[t]. Policy p receives t, the previous loss functions (ℓ_i)_{i<t}, H_t, and the whole current function ℓ_t; it returns g_t. S_{t+1}=S_t+||g_t||²; η_t=αD/√(S_t+||g_t||²). Append y_t to H_t, where y_t=x_t if g_t=0 and y_t=P_V(x_t−η_t g_t) otherwise. P_V denotes the project operation. Thus x_t is determined before receiving ℓ_t, while g_t and η_t may depend on ℓ_t. No algorithm here is assumed to observe future losses. Division in Lean ℝ is total: v/0=0, including 0/0. A zero gradient after positive energy can therefore coexist with a nonzero η_t.
blindSetup.notation: d_t²=||x_t−u||², δ_t(u)=(ℓ_t(x_t)).toReal−(ℓ_t(u)).toReal, R_T(u)=Σ_{0≤t<T}δ_t(u), q_t=||g_t||². EReal.toReal maps finite numbers to their real values; at either infinity its value is 0. ∂f(z)=SourceSubdifferential f z. SD_V(f)=SubdifferentiableOn V f; CX(f)=IsConvexExtended f. L_T means ∀0≤t<T, g_t∈∂ℓ_t(x_t), for the indicated run. Dom_D means ∀x∈V ∀y∈V, ||x−y||≤D. SD_T, CX_T abbreviate ∀0≤t<T, SD_V(ℓ_t) and ∀0≤t<T, CX(ℓ_t), respectively. Canon=canonicalPolicy. All time-indexed quantities, including L_T and benchmark energy, use the exact same parameter choices as their row unless distinguished with a prime or superscript.
blindSetup.benchmark: B(A,S,η)=OnlineOptimalStep.upperBound A S η; M(D,S)={b∈ℝ | ∃η∈ℝ, η>0 and b=B(D²,S,η)}. inf denotes sInf, GLB means lower bound greater than or equal to every other lower bound. Positivity of the candidate η is strict. This optimizes an upper-bound expression evaluated on the supplied energy; no time-varying or counterfactual policy optimum is asserted. The supplied helper definition is B(A,S,η)=A/(2η)+ηS/2.
blindSetup.unit4: a=(3,1,3,2,1,1,…), w=(0,1,1,2,2,…), s=(-3,-2,-4,7,7,…), e=(0,5,5,…), indexed from 0; s denotes signed, e denotes terminal. F_n(a,w)=Σ_{0≤t<n}(a_t−a_{t+1})w_t; a scalar weight in F means the constant sequence.
blindSetup.unit5: Here E=ℝ, V denotes the imported unitInterval, W has carrier {0} with its nonempty, closed, convex witnesses. b_t=3 for t=1, −4 for t=3, and 0 otherwise. ℓ_t(z)=b_t z embedded into EReal. Policy p returns b_t irrespective of its history and losses. ℓ'_t=ℓ_t for t<2 and ℓ'_t(z)=7 otherwise. ℓ⁰ and p⁰ are identically 0. Unless explicitly overridden use V, D=1, x_init=1/2, ℓ,p. x_t^α,S_t^α,η_t^α abbreviate x α t, q α t, r α t; R_T^α(u) denotes regret in this same run.
blindSetup.geometry: A domain V is a nonempty closed convex subset of E. P_V(z) is the classically chosen point of V whose distance to z is the infimum of distances from z to points of V. Unit 5 uses V=[0,1].
blindSetup.convexAnalysis: For f:E→EReal, ∂f(x)={g∈E | ∀y∈E, f(x)+ι(⟨g,y−x⟩)≤f(y)}, with the inequality in the extended reals. SourceProper(f) means ∀x, f(x)≠−∞ and ∃x∈E ∃r∈ℝ, f(x)=ι(r). SD_V(f) means SourceProper(f) and ∀x∈V, ∂f(x) is nonempty. CX(f) means convexity over ℝ of {(x,r)∈E×ℝ | f(x)≤ι(r)}. The support inequality tests every y∈E, even when subdifferentiability is required only on V.
blindSetup.policies: A SupportPolicy maps (t, Fin(t)→(E→EReal), Fin(t+1)→E, E→EReal) to E. OracleLaw(V,p) requires for all such t,past,H,f that SD_V(f) and H[t]∈V imply p(t,past,H,f)∈∂f(H[t]); the past and history need not be generated by a particular run. Canon ignores past losses, and returns a classically chosen element of ∂f(H[t]) if nonempty, otherwise zero.

comparison.name: weighted_potential_sum
comparison.sourceAssessment: An abstract summation lemma with signed inputs, freely chosen final a_T and nonnegative, possibly equal weights. Numeric preterminal specialization recovers printed14 with both halves and its endpoint.

blindReconstruction.meaning: The weighted differences are bounded using the last weight on both terms. The cap only covers the first T entries of a; the terminal value a_T is unrestricted.

blindReconstruction.meaning: D√S is the greatest lower bound over positive constant steps, including both boundary axes. This asserts a GLB, without requiring a positive minimizer.

blindReconstruction.assumptions: D,S∈ℝ with D≥0 and S≥0.
blindReconstruction.meaning: The quantity D√(2S) equals √2 times the infimum of the fixed-positive-step expression, including the zero cases.

blindReconstruction.assumptions: D,S∈ℝ with D≥0 and S≥0.
blindReconstruction.meaning: A positive step attains D√S precisely in the positive interior or at the origin. On an axis with only one zero coordinate there is no positive attaining step.

comparison.name: benchmark_positive_minimum
comparison.sourceAssessment: Exactly the positive-pair unique minimum from the source benchmark; every positive step attains in the separate identically-zero case.

blindReconstruction.assumptions: D,S∈ℝ with D>0 and S>0.
blindReconstruction.meaning: The proposed step is positive and attains the bound. For every positive step its bound is at least this large, and equality occurs exactly at the proposed step.
blindReconstruction.latex: \eta_*:=D/\sqrt S;\quad 0<\eta_*\ \land\ B(D^2,S,\eta_*)=D\sqrt S\ \land\ \forall\eta>0,\ [D\sqrt S\le B(D^2,S,\eta)\ \land\ (B(D^2,S,\eta)=D\sqrt S\iff\eta=\eta_*)]

comparison.name: source_theorem4_14_infimum
comparison.sourceAssessment: Original regret inequality unchanged. Equality is between the numerical upper bound and sqrt2 times an infimum at the same actual trajectory energy; mixed-zero cases deliberately correct the printed minimum.

blindReconstruction.assumptions: α=√2/2,D≥0, x_init∈V, CX_T, SD_T, L_T, Dom_D, u∈V; arbitrary p,T≥0.

slots: Two scalar sequences a,w on naturals, real bound C and positive natural T.
For all t<T: weights nonnegative, a_t<=C. Consecutive weights nondecreasing before T. No condition on terminal a_T.
C and a_t may be signed; weights may be zero or stall. This scalar generalization drops geometric prerequisites after reduction.
In OSD a_t=||x_t-u||², C=D² and w_t=sqrt(S_{t+1})/(2 α D). The 1/2 in the book is retained.
Deterministic summation; independent of any loss stream.
T=0 handled by regret proof separately. Source proof is an exact telescope followed by an inequality; no source correction.

transition.names: Domain SupportPolicy state history energy output selected eta LegalFeedback regret state_succ state_prefix energy_succ output_succ energy_eq_sum eta_eq_energy energy_nonneg energy_step_mono energy_pos_of_selected_ne_zero eta_pos_of_selected_ne_zero
slots: Real finite-dimensional inner-product model of Euclidean space, genuine bounded-domain projection when an update is taken, extended-real losses. State stores the played prefix and squared-norm sum.
Every trajectory defined for a fixed policy, start, loss stream and scales. Prefix invariance requires same policy, start and parameters and identical loss functions strictly before t.
Definitions themselves are total even without legal feedback; performance theorems impose legality and domain regularity. Positivity of step at nonzero selection requires α,D>0.
State appends current output if g=0, else projected output minus scaled current support. Energy is sum of norms squared for s<t; current rate uses energy through t.
η_t=α D/sqrt(S_{t+1}) in zero-based notation; source rate at nonzero update agrees. Dividing by zero gives Lean zero, but skip makes division causally irrelevant to the update.

Output before reading current whole loss; selection can use prior full losses, played outputs and current loss. Projection/next prediction use the resulting support, with no future loss, horizon or comparator passed to transition; policy may encode exogenous parameters.

At later zero with positive past energy η is generally nonzero, yet prediction holds. Scalar totalization never licenses a positive active step at D=0. Prefix equality at t says nothing about selected feedback at t if current losses differ.
Nonempty closed convex domain in finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Source subgradients are global affine supports, not relative normal-cone selection.
All points in stored history from feasible x1 lie in V. For any comparator u in V, outputs and comparator have finite loss on admissible rounds.
SubdifferentiableOn includes properness and existence of support everywhere on V. Properness is printed in Def. 2.20; weak epigraph convexity alone would not exclude identically +∞ or −∞.
Feasibility and EReal = coerced real at both evaluations. OracleLaw suffices for run legality; canonical noncomputable support choice is a particular legal policy.
No weakened coefficient or rate introduced.
Legality is needed only on the realized path of the stated run. It quantifies chosen subgradients, not a data-dependent regret certificate supplied as a premise.
CanonicalPolicy is mathematical choice, without computational or probabilistic oracle claims. EReal.toReal is exact on these finite values.

steps.anchor: Lemma 2.31 p19; Alg 2.2 p20; zero skip in 4.3,4.14
slots: Domain, current actual output, actual selected global support, feasible comparator, projected next output.
For every positive α,D on a nonzero selected round the η-scaled chain holds; one_step also allows a zero round. Separate singleton result covers D=0.
Subdifferentiability and legal current feedback; singleton path only needs feasible start, comparator, diameter bound zero, with no loss regularity for equality at identical points.
Signed loss gap <= inner gap <= potential decrement + energy in scaled chain. Skip gives equal next state and gap <=0. Singleton gives exact zero regret and terminal distance.
Chain keeps both halves and η_t²/2. Unscaled expression uses sqrt(S_{t+1})/(2αD) and αD/2. No division by an allegedly positive zero prefix.
Each update uses feedback after prediction; nonzero policy output in a singleton can have genuine positive energy.

Zero support need not mean equal losses (it only implies nonpositive gap). Proof of singleton equality alone uses totalized real regret even on inadmissible loss; publication guarantee additionally derives finite evaluations.

regret.anchor: Unnumbered p14 residual, Eq.4.4 and first inequality Thm 4.14 p40
slots: Same Euclidean model and one actual policy trajectory. Pairwise diameter bound D, independent of horizon and comparator.
Every feasible start, T, legal realized support sequence and comparator in same V. Specializations use two different runs α=1 or α=sqrt2/2.
Regularity on t<T and global convexity at the source-facing wrappers. Internal regret_bound can omit explicit convexity via actual supports; source wrappers reintroduce it.
Actual regret ≤ (1/(2α)+α)D sqrt(S_T) − ||x_T−u||² sqrt(S_T)/(2αD); removing the nonnegative residual yields source bounds.
Eq.4.4 constant 3/2; Thm4.14 constant sqrt(2), expressed D sqrt(2 S_T). Upper bound D may exceed actual diameter.
No expectation, martingale or assumption of future gradient knowledge. Every S is realized on that same trajectory; E endpoints use natural range T.

T=0, D=0 and S_T=0 retained. Eq.4.4 is derived on p39 starting with linear losses and extends to convex subdifferentiable losses via actual supports. Literal printed terminal benchmark is handled separately.

benchmark.anchor: p39 fixed-rate comparator and p40 second equality of Thm4.14
slots: Nonnegative real D,S; positive-real image of U(η)=D²/(2η)+ηS/2. Application uses S_T selected on the same tuned run.
For all D,S>=0 characterize GLB and existence of an attaining strictly positive η; for positive data quantify over every η to get uniqueness.
No positivity of both coefficients on the regret theorem. Strict positivity appears only for the unique optimizer formula.
GLB =D sqrt S and D sqrt(2S)=sqrt2 inf U; attain iff both positive or both zero. Full theorem joins the original regret inequality and separately repaired equality.
UpperBound argument D², normalized factors 1/2, outside sqrt2 exactly as printed. Unique positive optimizer D/sqrt S.
The η in inf is a hindsight comparison over an algebraic expression at the realized energy, not the rate sequence or regret obtained by rerunning with each η.
Mixed-zero cases admit no positive minimizer; both zero admits all. Preserve source wording, expose mathematical repair and independent review, with no author erratum claim.

tests.names: loss_regular feedback_energy trace_canary performance_canary prefix_canary zero_energy_canary zero_diameter_canary leading_zero_and_stall signed_zero_and_free_terminal
slots: Concrete real line, unit interval or singleton, affine losses; two separate scalar-potential witnesses.
Specific numerical trajectories; loss_regular quantifies t and domain, feedback/energy checks α and T, prefix compares two loss sequences.
